paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus is the one doing the healing, and He does it so people will turn to Him. Peter says it right to Aeneas: "Jesus Christ heals you!" (Acts 9:34). Peter is the messenger. Jesus is the power. And look at what happens next: all who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw Aeneas up and "turned to the Lord" (Acts 9:35).

Same thing in Joppa. Peter prays, he says "Tabitha, get up!" (Acts 9:40), and she opens her eyes. Then the news gets around, and "many people believed in the Lord" (Acts 9:42). I'm not going to pretend I know why every miracle happens, but this passage tells me what these two did: they led people to the Lord. A miracle in this passage is never the end of the story. It's a signpost, and the signpost points at Jesus.

Now here's the part for you, baker. Dorcas was "always occupied with works of kindness and charity" (Acts 9:36), and the widows stood there showing Peter the clothing she made (Acts 9:39). Nobody said, "Look at her résumé." They held up what her hands had made, and it said everything. You may never get a Peter-sized moment, but you get to be kind with your hands today, and Jesus is still the One who holds the whole story.
